## Informal description

There is a universal $0<\varepsilon_0\leq 1/200$ such that every sufficiently fine neck/cap cover has the corrected Appendix A topology: separating central spheres produce balanced tubes, whole neck covers produce either tubes or $S^2$-bundles over $S^1$, connected local covers have one of the six compatible cap/neck regions, and whole covers have one of the four global alternatives. Separation is relative to the neck's connected component, two-cap and doubly capped overlap conditions remain distinct, and chain no-return excludes a genuine neighborhood of the negative end.

## Informal proof

For A.20, take the minimum of the separating-tube, local-separation and sphere-bundle thresholds. Then take the minimum of the A.19, A.20 and compatible-local-region thresholds. This number is positive and at most $1/200$, independently of every manifold, metric, or cover.

For A.19 apply the separating-tube producer. For A.20, local agreement and connectedness give uniform separation labels for every supplied neck. In the separating case A.19 gives the exact source-selected tube, whose carrier is the whole manifold; in the nonseparating case the sphere-bundle producer gives the exact bundle certificate. Apply the local-region producer for A.21 and its whole-cover reduction for A.25, retaining all parameter and cap bounds.

The argument uses the proved assembly in [[node:compatible-neck-cap-regions]], including its smooth ball-filling construction. The A.19, local-separation, [[node:nonseparating-neck-covers-form-sphere-bundles]] and [[node:local-nonseparating-neck-covers-form-regions]] producers are proved.
